key_insight: SSFR calibrates synthetic imaging surrogates against observed target images to estimate spatially varying covariate effects more precisely while remaining robust to surrogate–target regression discrepancies.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables generative imaging models to support statistical inference when target scans are only partially observed, rather than treating synthetic scans as real measurements.
method: Use two-stage functional regression to calibrate surrogate information against observed target images.
Screen candidate surrogates using voxelwise residual explanatory power R²(z) together with the target-image observation rate.
Construct simultaneous confidence corridors using a weighted bootstrap.
evidence_signal: Simulations assessed accuracy and robustness, including neural-network-generated surrogates; an ADNI PET application produced uniformly narrower confidence corridors and a larger region of simultaneously significant age-related metabolic decline than observed-PET-only analysis.
watch_item: Efficiency gains depend on surrogate informativeness and the observation rate; robustness to regression discrepancies does not imply protection against arbitrary missing-data mechanisms.
paper_title: Synthetic Surrogate Functional Regression (SSFR): A Robust Framework for Estimating Spatially Varying Covariate Effects in Surrogate-Augmented Neuroimaging
